top_choice_rationale: P001 (Pakes, Berry, Levinsohn; B001) rewards a mature, well-tested measurement advance: random-coefficients demand estimation with endogenous prices, built on Berry's inversion and the 1995 jointly authored paper, together with the Ericson-Pakes dynamic-industry framework. It made substitution patterns, markups, merger effects and welfare counterfactuals recoverable from market data, which earlier reduced-form work could not do. It has been used for about three decades in academic work and regulatory practice and has spread into trade, health and environmental economics. The credit unit is compact and the three-laureate cap does not split the defining paper. Reservations remain: toolkit versus discovery, the exclusion of Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard and Levin, and the sensitivity of applied results to numerical implementation, instruments and functional form. These are qualifications that the citation should reflect, not grounds for no award. The slate offers only this one award proposal, and I judge it clearly preferable to P000.
recusal_note: No profile-based tie to Pakes, Berry or Levinsohn is apparent. I have co-authored with committee colleagues Krusell, Boppart and Friberg and am an IIES colleague of Krusell and Boppart. The 2018 Scientific Background cites my own climate work. None of this involves the P001 laureates. As chair I am an explicit B001 supporter, so agreement among colleagues who share my ties should not be read as independent confirmation.
